h1: Playground Equipment for Primary and Pre-Primary Schools

props.title: Playground Equipment for Primary and Pre-Primary Schools
props.summaryText: What pre-primary and primary children need from a playground, how to separate the two, and sample equipment lists you can take to a supplier.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: School playground with wooden play towers, swings and tyre climbers between school buildings

takeaways.text: Pre-primary children need low, simple equipment that builds basic movement skills; primary children need height and challenge.
Give each group its own zone, separated by a path, planting or a change in surface colour.
Pre-primary equipment should include ground-level play: panels, sand, tunnels and spring riders.
Primary children need climbing, swinging, spinning and balancing, plus open ground for running games.

faq.q: What playground equipment is suitable for pre-primary children?
faq.a: Low play stations with platforms under about a metre, 3 ft slides, spring riders, toddler swings, crawl tunnels, low climbers with gentle steps, balance paths close to the ground, sand play and play panels.

faq.q: What playground equipment is suitable for primary school children?
faq.a: Multi play stations with 5 ft slides, climbing walls and nets, monkey bars, balance beams and bridges, swings, see-saws, merry-go-rounds or spinners, and rotating climbers for older children.

faq.q: Should pre-primary and primary children share a playground?
faq.a: They can share a site, but should have separate zones. Older children move faster and use equipment differently, and younger children are easily knocked over. Separate zones also let you choose the right heights and surfaces for each group.
